scope: Corollary 6.1 (The sharp complete polynomial inequality for matrices) of the manuscript “The complete Crouzeix theorem: optimal similarity and a common positive boundary representation” (preprints/The-complete-Crouzeix-theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 325 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b5e37fffcae2be84), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every pair of positive integers n, m, every A ∈ Mn(C), every nonnegative integer d, and every choice of matrices B0, . . . , Bd ∈ Mm(C), the polynomial P(z) = Pd j=0 Bjzj satisfies ∥P[A]∥ = d X j=0 Aj ⊗ Bj ≤ 2 max z∈W(A) ∥P(z)∥. The constant is independent of both matrix sizes and the degree. No smaller constant holds uniformly over these choices.
